text.p: Brisbane broker Wilson HTM Ltd said it was gold producer Resolute Samantha as a buy, reflecting potential for an increase in reserves.

"Buy Resolute Samantha. Look for a re-rating based on reserves increases, exploration results and future production profile," Wilson's director of resources research, Phil Hutchings, said in a report.
"The company is now poised for substantial production growth," Hutchings said.
This would mainly come from new projects in Africa with Resolute's 1999 equity gold production likely to be 450,000 ounces based on its new African mines, Hutchings said.
"The recent acquisition of two high-quality open cut gold projects in Ghana and Tanzania has changed the company's portfolio profile," Hutchings said.
The N'Kran Hill mine in Ghana in which Resolute has an 82.5 percent interest, was scheduled to be producing gold in June, 1997, Hutchings said.
"Further favourable news is expected which could include an increase in reserves for N'Kran Hill from the current 700,000 ounces," Hutchings said.
Resolute's equity production from Ghana in 1998 would be 105,000 ounces at a cash cost of US$220 an ounce, he said.
The recent purchase of a 50 percent interest in Tanzania's Golden Pride project was made at a price of US$42 per reserve ounce, "a low acquisition cost," Hutchings said.
Golden Pride was expected to produce 170,000 ounces a year when fully operational in 1999 from a total gold resource of 2.4 million ounces, he said.
"In addition, Resolute's exploration portfolio in Australia is producing some exciting results," Hutchings said.
Resolute's attributable gold production totalled 241,806 ounces in the year to June, up from 101,998 a year earlier.
The company's shares have traded between A$2.50 and A$3.67 this year. The stock closed at A$2.64 on Monday, down six cents.
